_doc: How to read backend/co-ordination/. Written from `python -m app.scripts.inspect_datasets` output (see data/generated/dataset_manifest.json). The four official CSVs have NO header row; each row is: <layer>, x1, y1, x2, y2, ..., <trailing fields>. Layers are keyed by the first column so files can be renamed safely. A coordination_mapping.json placed inside a co-ordination folder overrides keys here (used by test fixtures).
coordinate_order_evidence: first value of every pair is 90.3-90.6 (> 90, so it cannot be a latitude); second is 23.7-23.9

DhakaStreet.notes: Road centre-line segments. attr_flag_raw is 0 on every row (meaning unknown, possibly a one-way flag). attr_cost_raw is ~2.40 x the geometry length in km (p05 2.39, p95 2.52), which matches travel minutes at ~25 km/h, but this is UNCONFIRMED, so it is kept raw and not used as a time.

DhakaBusBikolpo.evidence: layer name DhakaBusBikolpo, file Routemap-BikolpoBus.csv; line name inferred from those, provider not stated

DhakaBusUttara.evidence: layer name DhakaBusUttara, file Routemap-UttaraBus.csv; line name inferred from those, provider not stated

DhakaMetroRail.evidence: layer name DhakaMetroRail; MRT6 code follows the project brief route_id example
